Order 
The appellant has filed this third criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 11.08.2025 passed in Bail Application No.1959/2025 by the Special Judge, SC/ST (POA) Act, Chhatarpur (M.P.), whereby his bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023, has been rejected.

sentences.text: 2. The appellant has been arrested on 14.12.2023 relating to FIR/Crime No.251/2023 registered at Police Station Gulganj, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST Act.
3. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of present appellant has submitted that the present appellant is in custody since 14.12.2023, which is around 1 year and 9 months.

It is also submitted that the first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 10.07.2024 passed in CRA No.7564 of 2024 granting liberty to revive the same after examination of prosecutrix before the learned trial Court.
The prosecutrix has been examined on 12.07.2024.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50658 2 CRA-8985-2025 Thereafter, second bail application was wrongly filed challenging the previous order, which was also dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 03.07.2025 passed in CRA No.9968 of 2024.
Thereafter, he moved before the learned trial and after rejection of bail application vide the impugned order, he has filed this bail application/criminal appeal before this Court.

4. It is further submitted by the counsel for present appellant that though the prosecutrix in her statement has supported the story or prosecution, but it is revealed from her cross-examination that her husband went to the field for irrigating which is adjacent to her home.

sentences.text:
Though the DNA and FSL reports are positive,
but it is a matter of consent.

Therefore, keeping in view the long custody as well as the liberty granted while dismissing the first bail application which has been fulfilled, so also looking to the facts revealed from the cross-examination of prosecutrix, the present appellant is entitled to be released on bail.
The present appellant is only 22 years old.
He has no criminal antecedents.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
In view of the aforesaid submissions, it is prayed that the appellant may be released on bail.
5 . Per contra , learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer of bail and prayed for rejection of appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.
Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the attending facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50658 3 CRA-8985-2025 appeal is allowed and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.
